chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Amriki, from Ali ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I saw my brothers Musa, Ishaq, and Muhammad, sons of Ja'far (peace be upon him), giving the salutation (taslim) in the prayer to the right and to the left: 'Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah, peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah.'

key_terms.الْسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّه: Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah
key_terms.بَنِي جَعْفَرٍ: sons of Ja'far (referring to the Imams' brothers)
key_terms.عَنِ الْيَمِينِ وَالشِّمَالِ: to the right and to the left
key_terms.يُسَلِّمُونَ: giving the salutation (taslim) at the end of prayer

ai.seo_question: How did the Ahl al-Bayt perform the taslim (salutation) at the end of the prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from the Ahl al-Bayt highlights the Sunnah of the Prophet’s family in performing the final salutations (taslim) of the prayer, affirming the practice of turning to the right and left while reciting 'Peace be upon you and the mercy of Allah.' It serves as a key evidence in Shia jurisprudence for the recommended manner of concluding the prayer, emphasizing the familial transmission of ritual precision from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq to his sons.
